subject: Pathfinder MAP: evaluation milestones & GPU pool sizing
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@veridian.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sat, May 16, 2026 at 9:12 AM -0700
Subject: Pathfinder MAP: evaluation milestones & GPU pool sizing

Sanjay —

Great to sync earlier. Attached is a first-draft MAP and a simple sizing spreadsheet (pathfinder-map-v1.xlsx) that lays out the evaluation milestones, acceptance criteria, and a preliminary GPU pool recommendation for Dedicated/Private. High-level asks from Redwood:

- Confirm target production cutover window (we penciled in mid-June).
- Confirm which acceptance tests you want in-scope for the MAP (throughput, p95 latency, and a small quality sample we can run).
- Tell us if you have procurement/tranche restrictions that would block H100-equivalent commits in June–July.

What we propose in the draft (see sheet "Runway"):
- 2-week pilot (functional + perf microbenchmarks)
- 2-week scale eval (batching, KV cache behavior, steady-state throughput)
- Acceptance gate: p95 < 250ms for 1k concurrent requests and no more than 8% quality delta on the test prompts
- Reserve recommendation: start with 16 H100-equivalent slots, with burst to 64 for load tests and go-live ramp

If that looks reasonable I can convert this into a mutual-action timeline (owner, due date, acceptance artifact) and send a version for signatures. Can you confirm availability for a short follow-up on Monday?

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
(415) 555-0142

Subject: Re: Pathfinder MAP: evaluation milestones & GPU pool sizing

Jonas —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the draft. A few clarifying points before we lock the timeline: 

1) Lead times: Our procurement team has a preferred H100 vendor but the earliest tranche they can commit to is late July unless we do a partial commit. Is it possible to stage the pool so we do a smaller reserved tranche in June and add capacity later?
2) Sizing: Can you send an alternative that assumes 8-bit quantization so we can compare the cost/perf trade-offs?
3) Acceptance: We want to add a security/compliance checkpoint (SOC2 evidence) before final sign-off — will that block the go-live if delayed?

We can do Monday afternoon. Sanjay

Subject: Pathfinder MAP: updated timeline + sizing options

Sanjay —

Appreciate the fast follow-up. I updated the MAP with two concrete options (attached):

Option A — Conservative / procurement-friendly
- Reserve 8 H100-equivalent slots (June pilot tranche)
- Burst up to 32 for ramp and load tests (on-demand)
- Timeline: pilot May 25–June 7, scale eval June 8–21, acceptance window June 22–28, close target July 5

Option B — Aggressive / lower unit cost
- Reserve 32 H100-equivalent slots up front (June commit)
- Burst up to 64 for go-live
- Timeline: pilot May 25–June 1, scale eval June 2–15, acceptance window June 16–22, close target June 30

Quantization note: we included a worksheet that models 8-bit and 4-bit quantization trade-offs. Rough guidance: 8-bit reduces unit cost ~2.3x with a small latency improvement; 4-bit can cut cost further but requires an extra eval sweep for quality.

Security/compliance: SOC2 artifacts are not a hard blocker for the runtime commitment, but we recommend the SOC2 evidence be delivered before the acceptance window starts. If SOC2 is delayed past acceptance, we can defer final cutover and run in a restricted pilot mode (VPC + audit logging only).

Next steps I propose:
- Monday call to pick Option A vs B and confirm procurement constraints (30 minutes)
- Redwood to finalize mutual-action plan (owners + acceptance artifacts) and share DocuSign link for the reservation term
- Marissa to confirm budget/credit approvals and Priyom to coordinate on deployment handoff

Can you confirm Monday 3:00 PM PT for the call?

—Jonas
